title: AWS Step Functions Error-Rate Trend Anomaly
app: AWS Step Functions execution events via CloudWatch/EventBridge to the Splunk Add-on for AWS.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=aws:states:execution
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as events, sum(eval(status="FAILED" OR status="TIMED_OUT")) as errors by _time
| eval error_rate=round(100*errors/events,2)
| eventstats avg(error_rate) as avg_rate, stdev(error_rate) as sd_rate
| where error_rate>avg_rate+3*sd_rate
| sort - _time
description: Baselines the hourly error rate for AWS Step Functions and flags hours where it spikes more than three standard deviations above normal, catching emerging instability before it becomes an outage.
value: An error-rate spike is the earliest signal that AWS Step Functions is degrading; statistical baselining suppresses routine noise and pages only on genuine anomalies.
implementation: Ingest AWS Step Functions logs into index=bi; schedule every 15 minutes over a trailing window and alert on 3-sigma error-rate anomalies.
visualization: Timechart of AWS Step Functions error rate with anomaly band.

references.title: AWS Step Functions — Monitoring with CloudWatch

grandmaExplanation: We learn what a normal amount of AWS Step Functions errors looks like and warn you only when something is genuinely going wrong.
